result.summary: Diagnosed GH-592 / ISS-0625. Three independent root causes, all part of the issue's stated scope; no incidental new defects found. LUA-12: deferral, ServiceCatalog has zero callers, non-simulation branch hardcoded. LUA-15: anti-forgery pattern from host_context.zig not applied to fail.zig; three _G globals script-writable and unread. LUA-16: captureStackTrace unimplemented, ScriptErrorPayload has zero construction sites, and instruction_count + memory_peak_bytes fields have no source until LUA-08 and LUA-09 land in the same run. Two design decisions flagged for CODE-DESIGNER (LUA-12 ServiceCatalog scope; LUA-12 return shape). Fix sequencing documented: LUA-15 first, then LUA-12 in parallel (independent), then LUA-16 last, with the explicit constraint that LUA-16 ScriptErrorPayload construction MUST be skipped if LUA-08/09 do not land in the same run. Diagnosis YAML and ISS-0625 file written; GitHub comment posted with rco-sync-ref. No source code modified.

issues.description: CODE-DESIGNER must decide: does ServiceCatalog become a field on ExecutionContext (design §17.1 path, requires real HTTP implementation) OR is LUA-12 explicitly scoped as simulation-only (annotated IN_PROGRESS with simulation-only note)? Either is acceptable; the decision is irreversible for this run.

CODE-DESIGNER must decide: return a single response table per design §17.1 (breaking change for any script using `local body, status = platform.call_service(...)`) OR keep the tuple and represent errors as a separate error table on the side.

CODE-DESIGNER must plan: if LUA-08 and LUA-09 do NOT land in the same WF-03 run as LUA-16, the ScriptErrorPayload construction MUST be skipped entirely (instruction_count and memory_peak_bytes would always read 0, which is a misleading test outcome). CaptureStackTrace itself is independent of LUA-08/09 and can still land.
